annotations.title: The wordes of the Gatherer.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> Some Interpreters take theſe foure Hebrew wordes, Agur, Iache, Ithiel, and Ual, conteined in this firſt verſe, to be proper names of men, ſuppoſing that a certaine wiſeman named Agur, the ſonne of Iache, ſpake the ſentences folowing in this chapter, to his ſonnes or ſchollars, called Ithiel & Ual. And ſo this ſuppoſed Agur, not Salomon, should be the auctor of this chapter. But the old Interpreter, whom S. Ierom approueth and foloweth, tranſlated the ſame wordes as nounes appellatiues. Neither doth anie ancient Father account this Agur, amongſt the writers of holie Scriptures. And if there were a peculiar auctor of this chapter, it is like the ſame ſhould haue bene placed laſt, and not before that which now foloweth, and is by al men confeſſed to be Salomons. And therfore we thinke it more probable, with S. Beda, and the common opinion, that there was no other auctor of anie part of this booke, beſides King Salomon. VVho is here called <sc>CONGREGANS</sc>, the Gatherer, <mn>[2]</mn> becauſe he gathered theſe excellent Parables, and Prouerbes; as the ſonne of the Holie Ghoſt, ſignified by the word <sc>IACHE</sc>, povvring forth diuine ſentences, for inſtruction of <sc>ITHIEL</sc> & <sc>VCAL</sc>, that is, of al thoſe vvith vvhom God is by his grace, and vvho are ſtrengthened by God abiding vvith them.

notes.text: Some suppose one Agur to be author of this chapter. But it seemeth more probable that only Solomon is author of this whole book.

annotations.title: A bond woman when she shal be heyre.
annotations.text: Of al thinges in this world, it ſemeth moſt abſurde, that hereſie doth dominiere ouer Catholique religion: <mn>◦</mn> vvhich God ſome times, and in ſome places ſuffereth, for the greater merite of his elect.

notes.text: VVhy God suffereth heresie to reigne.
